proof: EnemyStats.spawnSpeedFactor retains its existing first two results and appends the original integer speed argument before global factors. EnemySim retains it by actor id across actual Charm conversion; no inverse reconstruction from rounded speed.

EnemySim.applyNativeBoost resolves hostile or friendly World by the actual id, checks source policy/alive/canBeBoosted before touching cache, reads the current source run wave and applies cached raw HP/contact/shot/speed bases via World.resetNativeStats.

Actual Triceratops with source-matching two-player factors starts102HP and resets/heals to256; raw contact yields2, not double-rounded3; original speed argument255 yields387px/s. A later zero modifier resets to102HP from the retained cache, not fresh changed player stats or a compounded boost.
Actual Charm conversion retains id, position, owner and source speed sample; cached boost heals the real friendly actor to256 without respawn or new lifetime.

Real boosted BloatedSpawner death creates five DireJunkies with updated unboosted global factors:22HP/2contact, not the boosted parent values or old debug99 multipliers. Shared nativeBases.spawn and spawnContexts are updated without inheriting boost percentages.

SeaPig boost refusal, dead/unknown actors and unported legacy kinds are rejected; refused boost does not warm an empty cache. Future evolution scene adapter must still apply flags/effects/attack reset after a valid live actor refuses its stat boost.
